_comment: TEMPLATE — do not copy this file into place by hand. Install it with `bash tools/install-hooks.sh`, which substitutes __REPO_ROOT__ for the real container root and MERGES these entries into the target settings file instead of overwriting it. Every entry is tagged 'novig-checkpoint-hooks'; the installer only ever replaces entries carrying that tag (or matching the generic tools/resume.sh /tools/autosave.sh /tools/hooks/ /tools/ckpt.sh /tools/capture_inbox.sh paths, so a sibling repo's own install of the same pattern is recognised too rather than duplicated), so a user's own permissions, env and other projects' hooks survive. WHY NOT THIS REPO'S OWN .claude/settings.json: Claude Code on the web does not load hooks from a repo that sits in a subdirectory of the session root when several repos share one container — CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is unset and one project root is resolved for the whole session. The commands below glob every repo under that root, so one install protects every checkpoint-managed project in the container, and each entry point aggregates all of them into ONE JSON object (see tools/hooks/emit.py — two objects do not parse, and that would silently cost the entire session briefing).

hooks.command: for f in __REPO_ROOT__/*/tools/hooks/brief.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && exec bash "$f"; done; true  # novig-checkpoint-hooks
hooks.statusMessage: Reading where the last session stopped...

hooks.command: for f in __REPO_ROOT__/*/tools/hooks/inbox.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && exec bash "$f"; done; true  # novig-checkpoint-hooks
for f in __REPO_ROOT__/*/tools/hooks/save.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && exec bash "$f"; done; true  # novig-checkpoint-hooks
for f in __REPO_ROOT__/*/tools/hooks/save.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && exec bash "$f"; done; true  # novig-checkpoint-hooks
for f in __REPO_ROOT__/*/tools/hooks/big.sh; do [ -f "$f" ] && exec bash "$f"; done; true  # novig-checkpoint-hooks
hooks.statusMessage: Session is large - saving before compaction...
